subject: Question - help on difference between local server and online server provided by R-studio

messages.author: 4c8d0fcf49835e37
messages.subject: Question - help on difference between local server and online server provided by R-studio
parts:
Hi, i am trying to pre-define a CSV file that contains a set of variable names, + some of these variable names have numbers that represent them.

In my local R-studio, on the server, i am able to read the csv file seperately, store it inside the workspace, and do something like this

##so this code is run outside of the R server##
config_file<-read.csv("C:\\Users\\Yi Xiang\\Desktop\\trial\\config.csv",header=TRUE,sep=",")
  config_names<-config_file[,1]
  config_values<-config_file[,2]
  n<-length(config_values)
#############################################

and then i define the following functions to run in the reactive outputs later on.

so my server, has functions like this

  first_entry<-function(){
    for(i in 1:n){
      if(!is.na(config_values[i]==TRUE)){
        return(i)
        break
      }
    }
  }
  FLAG<-first_entry()
  latest_names<-as.character(config_file[FLAG:n,1])
  latest_codes<-config_file[FLAG:n,2]
 
  n2<-length(latest_codes)
 
  return_position<-function(n)({
    for(i in 1:length(latest_codes)){
      if(latest_codes[i]==n){
        return(i)
        break
      }
    }
  })
 
  code_translate_to_shoptype<-function(data){
    empty_vector<-c(rep(1,length(data)))
    for(i in 1:length(data)){
      if(is.na(data[i])==TRUE){
        empty_vector[i]<-NA
      }
      else{
        empty_vector[i]<-as.character(latest_names[return_position(data[i])])
      }
    }
    return(empty_vector)
  }

while my UI.R has codes like this

    checkboxGroupInput("variables","Choose your column number", config_names)

#################

so running on the local server, it is perfectly okay. everything is running

however, if i use the Online R Studio, it doesnt work anymore, despite having the same work space, variables declared.

Also, i am not allowed to define things such as n<-length(#code)

how can i over come this problem in UI.R and Server.R?

Basically,

(1) how can i pre-store a data frame given a CSV file uploaded onto the online Rstudio, and be able to call it inside the UI.R to get my names out,

(2)and do certain simple assignments, variations, and other things in the R.server without crashing things or failure to run?

the purpose of this is i do not have to hard-define my names, and the subsequent user can just simply upload the config file containing the base information for easy update.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Question - help on difference between local server and online server provided by R-studio
parts:
You can put this code in a new file called global.R in the same directory as ui.R and server.R. Any code in global.R gets executed before ui.R and server.R, and it executes in the global environment so any variables/functions you define are accessible anywhere.

The one caveat to using global.R is that Shiny will not notice that it has changed and re-execute it, the way that ui.R and server.R do. That means that when running locally, if you make changes to global.R you'll need to stop and re-run runApp for the changes to take effect.

When running on Glimmer (or any other Shiny Server) you can't re-run runApp, so instead, if you change the last-modified-date of a file called restart.txt in your app directory, that will instruct Shiny Server to restart the app next time. (One easy way to do this is to log onto our RStudio Server and run the command system("touch restart.txt").)

On Tuesday, June 11, 2013 2:24:11 AM UTC+8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
You can put this code in a new file called global.R in the same directory as ui.R and server.R. Any code in global.R gets executed before ui.R and server.R, and it executes in the global environment so any variables/functions you define are accessible anywhere.

The one caveat to using global.R is that Shiny will not notice that it has changed and re-execute it, the way that ui.R and server.R do. That means that when running locally, if you make changes to global.R you'll need to stop and re-run runApp for the changes to take effect.

When running on Glimmer (or any other Shiny Server) you can't re-run runApp, so instead, if you change the last-modified-date of a file called restart.txt in your app directory, that will instruct Shiny Server to restart the app next time. (One easy way to do this is to log onto our RStudio Server and run the command system("touch restart.txt").)
